whatItIs.text: Wine fermented a second time into acetic acid — tart, dark, and made for vinaigrettes, pan sauces, and pickles.

historyNote.text: Vinegar-making is as old as brewing: the Babylonians were making it from wine, dates, and beer around 3000 BC, Greeks and Romans used wine vinegar constantly, and the French city of Orléans turned aging it into a formal craft — the Orléans process.

howToChoose.text: Choose vinegars that list red wine as the source and nothing else; anything under about 4-5% acidity tastes thin, and 'wine-flavoured' spirit vinegar is not the same thing.

storage.text: Keep sealed in a cool, dark cupboard — vinegar essentially keeps indefinitely.

useItUp.text: A splash deglazes a pan of onions, balances a rich stew, or pickles red onions in ten minutes; a dull bottle still works where acidity, not flavour, is the point.

substitutions.note: sweeter and darker; reduce it slightly for savoury dishes

substitutions.substitute: white wine vinegar + a little red wine
